exposure: Planned mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean)
outcome: Survival at discharge without severe morbidity
Survival at 2 years of corrected age without neurosensory impairment
cohort: 390 women with breech singleton pregnancies in France, born at 26-34 weeks of gestation after preterm labor or preterm prelabor rupture of membranes in 2011.
finding: Planned cesarean delivery was not associated with improved survival, survival without severe morbidity, or survival at 2 years without neurosensory impairment compared to planned vaginal delivery in preterm breech singletons.
mod_finding: Planned cesarean delivery was not associated with improved survival, survival without severe morbidity, or survival at 2 years without neurosensory impairment compared to planned vaginal delivery for preterm breech singletons born at 26-34 weeks of gestation after preterm labor or preterm prelabor rupture of membranes.
